key_insight: Training GPT-style models on synthetic limit order book streams shows they learn amortized Bayesian inference over latent market regimes, not just next-token statistics.
engineering_relevance: This suggests foundation models can be used as fast, frozen surrogates for regime estimation and simulator calibration in market microstructure workflows.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on order-flow sequences from simulators with known latent parameters.
Compare model predictions against Bayes-optimal and oracle references using exact entropy-aware evaluation.
Probe frozen activations for linearly decodable latent regimes and test transfer to real NASDAQ order flow.
evidence_signal: The models match the exact Bayes optimum to within a millinat per token, recover latent regimes from frozen activations, and improve zero-shot transfer when the simulator prior better covers real market flow.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on how well synthetic training regimes cover the target market, so poor simulator priors can limit transfer even when loss looks near-optimal.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
